deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a table of class groups of positive binary quadratic forms (Gauss's notation ax^2+2bxy+cy^2) of determinant D=-p, for primes p ≡ 1 (mod 8). The page covers p = 401 (end only), 409, 433, 449, 457 and 521; the next page continues with 569, 577, 593 and 601. For each p Gauss does three things.

(a) Class group layout. He writes the class indices in two rows:
  0 1 2 ... h/2
    h-1 h-2 ... h/2+1
so that each class k is set against its inverse h-k. This means the group of properly primitive classes is cyclic of order h, generated by class 1. The classes 0 and h/2 are the two ambiguous classes.
- 409: rows 0..8 / 16..9, so h = 16.
- 433: h = 12.
- 449: h = 20.
- 457: h = 8.
- 521: h = 32.
- The top three lines belong to p = 401 (h = 20), continued from the preceding page of the bundle.

(b) Three-square decompositions. Opposite each pair {k, h-k} with k even (the principal genus, i.e. the squares in the cyclic group) he enters one decomposition p = a^2+b^2+c^2. The listed pairs, all arithmetically correct:
- 401: Cl.8.12: 256+144+1; Cl.10: 196+196+9.
- 409: Cl.0: 400+9; Cl.2.14: 324+81+4; Cl.4.12: 256+144+9; Cl.6.10: 324+49+36; Cl.8: 144+144+121.
- 433: Cl.0: 289+144; Cl.2.10: 324+100+9; Cl.4.8: 225+144+64; Cl.6: 361+36+36.
- 457: Cl.0: 441+16; Cl.2.6: 225+196+36; Cl.4: 169+144+144.
- 521: Cl.0: 400+121; Cl.2.30: 289+196+36; Cl.4.28: 361+144+16; Cl.6.26: 484+36+1; Cl.8.24: 256+144+121 (continued overleaf).
- 449: the table is set up (Cl.0 to Cl.10) but left empty.

In every case the number of essentially distinct decompositions (unordered, unsigned, zeros allowed) equals the number of inverse-pairs in the principal genus, (h/4)+1. Equivalently r_3(p) = 12h(-4p). For example, for 409: 24 + 3*48 + 24 = 192 = 12*16. This is the correspondence of Disquisitiones Arithmeticae arts. 278-292 between representations by x^2+y^2+z^2 and binary classes of determinant -p.

(c) The 'c: q' entries. These record a prime q represented by (i.e. the first coefficient of a form in) the class in question. Examples:
- 433: Cl.1 contains 7, Cl.2 contains 17, Cl.4 contains 13.
- 457: Cl.1 contains 11, Cl.2 contains 17, Cl.4 contains 2.
- 521: Cl.1:3, Cl.3:23, Cl.4:53, Cl.5:19, Cl.6:37, Cl.7:7, Cl.8:101 and 113, Cl.9:43.

My checks: in each case (-p/q) = 1, so q is represented by some form of determinant -p. The genus character (q/p) is +1 exactly when the class index is even and -1 when it is odd. The prime 2 sits in the ambiguous class h/2, because (2,1,(p+1)/2) is ambiguous; Gauss records this for 457 here and for 521 overleaf. I did not verify the exact index of each class within the cyclic group, which depends on Gauss's choice of generator. The bare 'c' or 'c:' marks are apparently check marks.

Unclear: '45. 139.' under the 449 header is of unclear purpose.
errors: No arithmetic errors found. All three-square decompositions sum to the stated p, and every recorded prime q lies in a genus consistent with the parity of its class index (checked via Legendre symbols).

Visible overwritings are self-corrections, apparently ending at the correct values: 433 Cl.2.10 (324+100+9), 433 Cl.4.8 (225+144+64 with a cancelled entry before 13), 457 Cl.4 (169 written over another number), and 521 Cl.2.30 (196 written over 195).

results.what: Tabulation of the cyclic class groups of determinant -p for p = 401, 409, 433, 449, 457, 521 (h = 20, 16, 12, 20, 8, 32), with inverse classes paired
results.modern_name: Class groups Cl(-4p) of imaginary quadratic orders; cyclicity of class groups for prime discriminant
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae, 1801, arts. 305-307 on class-group tables)

results.what: Matching of decompositions p = a^2+b^2+c^2 with inverse-pairs of classes in the principal genus; count of decompositions = h/4 + 1, i.e. r_3(p) = 12h(-4p)
results.modern_name: Gauss's three-squares theorem / class-number formula for r_3(n)

results.what: Location of small primes q in specific classes, consistent with genus characters (q/p)
results.modern_name: Splitting of primes and Frobenius classes in the class group; genus theory

deep.surprise_reason: This is a computational table illustrating results Gauss published in the Disquisitiones: the class-group structure for determinant -p, the class-number count of three-square representations, and genus characters. The assignment of individual decompositions to individual classes anticipates modern interest in the class-group action on three-square representations, but Gauss's DA already describes such a correspondence. Nothing here goes beyond his known work.
